catalog_quote: Nota 7. El accenro comunmente fe ha[ze] enluyltima fallaba de las palabras, ó vozes de efta lengua : V .g. Pelé y el hombre : vacal y muger. Dixe comunmente, porque ay nombres, y verbos, que no tienen el acento largo en la vlcima fyllaba; para que fe conozca quando la palabra tenga el acento largo en vl cima fyllaba, ó letra vocal, pondremos fobrc ella vna tilde, que lo note. [scanned of 1732 print with long-s; reads: 'El accento comunmente se haze en la ultima syllaba de las palabras, o vozes de esta lengua: v.g. Pelé, el hombre: vacál, muger. Dixe comunmente, porque ay nombres, y verbos, que no tienen el acento largo en la ultima syllaba; para que se conozca quando la palabra tenga el acento largo en ultima syllaba, o letra vocal, pondremos sobre ella una tilde, que lo note.']

new_statements.quote: Machoni describes a relatively small inventory of sounds consisting of five vowels, a, e, i, o, u and a limited number of consonants. Stress is predominantly word-final.[fn.180] The symbol y is used as an equivalent of i, especially when stressed, but also for referring to a semi-consonant. [...] [fn.180:] Word-final accent is usually written with an acute by Machoni. The examples given are in Machoni's original spelling. [p.390:] The second-person-singular imperative ending consists of a vowel -y after roots ending in a consonant, and a lengthened final vowel after roots ending in a vowel. This is indicated by doubling of the last vowel. It is not sure whether the added vowel was pronounced separately, as vowel length, or that it was merely stressed.

Stress is predominantly word-final.180 The symbol y is used…
new_statements.relation_note: Same placement and type as the catalog record (Machoni 1732 Nota 7: accent commonly on the last syllable = fixed final): Adelaar summarises Machoni as 'Stress is predominantly word-final' and notes that Machoni writes the final accent with an acute. Adds only philological detail (grave on -ton, the doubled imperative vowel), no different rule. Consistent with the Zamponi 2008 reading already held by the project.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress in Lule (as recorded by Machoni 1732) falls predominantly on the final syllable; Machoni marks the word-final accent with an acute (occasionally a grave, fn.183 p.389, reason unknown). Adelaar's statement is a restatement of Machoni's Nota 7, the catalog's source.
new_statements.exceptions: 'predominantly' (not all words are final-stressed; no list given, mirroring Machoni's 'comunmente.. ay nombres, y verbos, que no tienen el acento largo en la ultima syllaba'); fn.183 p.389: participle -ton written with a grave (amaici-ton) instead of an acute, reason not known; p.390: vowel-final roots form the 2sg imperative by doubling the last vowel, and it is unsure whether this was a separate vowel, length, or mere stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Lule as documented by Antonio Machoni (Maccioni) de Cerdena, Arte y vocabulario de la lengua lule y tonocote (1732), i.e. the Lule of the Jesuit reductions near Tucuman (Machoni treats Lule and Tonocote as one language spoken by five 'nations': Tonocote, Lule, Ysistine, Toquistine, Oristine); Adelaar notes the Lule-Vilela relationship is probable but not close. All statements on stress for lule1238 derive from Machoni's single description.

(2) Deciding source: a 1732 Jesuit pedagogical grammar, but for an 18th-century-extinct isolate it is the sole primary attestation, so no fieldwork or instrumental source can exist; the question is only whether the best modern philological analysis agrees. Dixe comúnmente porque hay nombres y verbos que no tienen el acento largo en la última syllaba; para que se conozca quando la palabra tenga el acento largo en última syllaba o letra vocal, pondremos sobre ella una tilde que lo note.' tone.summary: No statement on tone or pitch. The work treats only word accent ('acento largo'): commonly word-final, marked in the spelling, with a reduced contrastive function (ísi 'urinate!' vs isí 'well').
